title: Conversation Latency Inspector: per-model & route breakdown with streaming/non-streaming slices
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: Build a single inspection dashboard and associated query surface that lets SRE/infra/ML teams slice latency by model, route (route = API endpoint + route config), and IO mode (streaming vs non-streaming). The view must show p50/p95/p99 and request counts, expose temporal trends, and link to traces and example slow/fast requests. Motivation: existing dashboards scatter these views across multiple boards and lack easy streaming/non-streaming splits and conversation-shape cohorts. This work will unify visibility for recent outages and support faster RCA.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Aggregated metrics (p50/p95/p99, count, error rate) per model-version and per route, with an explicit dimension for io_mode: streaming | non_streaming | hybrid.
- Breakdowns by conversation shape: single-turn, multi-turn (2-5), long-conversation (6+), and average prompt+response token counts.
- Time-series panels (last 30m, 24h, 7d) and percentile trend lines with anomaly highlights.
- Trace hooks: "Jump to trace" links for any cohort percentile bucket that open distributed trace view with the same filters applied.
- Example-finder table: sample successful and errored requests for selected percentile with request metadata (model, route, seq_len, client_id) and anonymized prompt hash.
- Alerting knobs: baseline SLI (p95) per model-route, and default thresholds + recommended warning/critical values.
- Performance: dashboard queries must run under 10s for 24h windows for a single model-route slice.
- Backfilled data for last 90 days using metrics pipeline (if full backfill impossible, document gaps).

Implementation plan:
1) Metrics schema: extend existing latency metric labels to include io_mode and conversation_bucket. Update exporters in serving runtime to emit io_mode on request completion span.
2) Tracing hooks: add link metadata to top-level response span for trace-id + sampling flag; ensure sampled slow requests always have full traces captured (sampling override for p99-ish).
3) Pipeline: update metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> ingest -> metrics-store) to rollup percentile histograms with tags {model, model_version, route, io_mode, conversation_bucket}. Coordinate with infra team to add pre-aggregation for high-cardinality routes.
4) Dashboards: author new panels in Observability Console (Console: Latency Inspector) plus a lightweight JSON query endpoint for ad-hoc cohort queries.
5) Runbook: attach an RCA playbook with actions for common patterns (kernel contention, KV cache warmup, network stall, model fallbacks).
6) Rollout: deploy tracing hooks and pipeline changes to non-prod, validate with synthetic load (script: tools/latency-synth), then staged rollout to production.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Adding io_mode increases cardinality; mitigate by limiting which routes include io_mode (only LLM routes) and pre-aggregating common model-route combinations.
- Full percentile accuracy vs storage: use HDR and rolling histograms with controlled retention.

Data privacy: request payloads must not be stored; sample IDs and anonymized prompt hashes only. Conformance with privacy policy required for example-finder samples.
